theorem.statement: MVW2012 Theorem 1 (p.2): optimal simple counterfeiting attack on Wiesner's scheme succeeds with probability exactly (3/4)^n.
theorem.citation: A. Molina, T. Vidick, J. Watrous. Optimal counterfeiting attacks and generalizations for Wiesner's quantum money. TQC 2012, LNCS 7582, 45-64. arXiv:1202.4010v1
theorem.quantifier: sup over ALL quantum channels (CPTP maps, unbounded ancilla and computation) from one note to two notes
assumptions: Bank note = n qubits, each uniformly and independently one of |0>,|1>,|+>,|-> (secret to the adversary).
Adversary receives exactly ONE valid note and applies any quantum channel to output two notes (simple counterfeiting).
No access to a verification oracle; no repeated or adaptive verification; no leaked post-measurement states (MVW2012 p.2 explicitly excludes these).
Bank verifies each candidate independently with the exact projective test (all n qubits must be correct; zero error tolerance, no loss).
caveats: Not a bound for noisy/threshold verifiers (that is game W2), lossy channels, oracle access, or S-money.
Does not cover the classical-verification variant (P-W1CV) and must not be used for it.

parameters.n: number of qubits per note, integer >= 1

optimization.reason: Resource optimisation (choosing N, thresholds and analysis variables to minimise photons under all targets) is the certificate compiler, lane I. It runs offline (reports/optimizer_working) and is not wired into the studio; its apparent photon savings do not survive calibration uncertainty. Nothing here searches parameters.
